recipes.name: 2-Step Inside-Out Chicken Pot Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut-up
1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Chicken Soup (Regular or 98% Fat Free)
1 (16 ounce) package frozen vegetable combination (broccoli, cauliflower, carrots)

steps.text: Cook chicken in nonstick skillet until browned, stirring often.
Add soup and vegetables. Cover and simmer until done. Serve on biscuits.

raw_recipe.headline: 2-Step Inside-Out Chicken Pot Pie
raw_recipe.description: This simply delicious skillet dish features a tasty combination of cooked chicken, mixed vegetables and Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Chicken Soup, heated together and served over hot biscuits.

review.reviewBody: I loved this! I used fresh carrots, broccoli, mushrooms, and frozen corn and used 2 cans of cream of chicken soup. Both my husband and I loved it! I also added some celery salt, garlic powder, and paprika- a couple shakes of each. SO good! And you can adjust it to whatever you like! Yum yum.

I followed the directions, but added another can of soup. I omitted the broccoli, but added canned corn, peas and carrots. I also found it a bit bland, so added a bit of parsley, celery salt, and onion powder. I didn't have biscuits, so I used flaky pastry puffs. I halved the puffs, poured the mixture on top of it and put in the oven at 350 F for 15 minutes (covered with foil to avoid drying up). It was yummy!

Very easy and good. Instead of making biscuit I put every thing in a cassarole dish and poured bisquick mix over it and baked it for 35 min. Once you do that it is the same recipe that is on the back of the bisquick box. Will be making again

This recipe was great ! Quick & easy although I switched some things a bit. I added garlic salt & pepper when I sautéed the chicken & then I used a can of cream of chicken along with a can of cream of mushroom. Put it all baking dish & topped everything with buisquik to make a crust on top . Baked it at 350 for about 40 mins or until it's nice & golden brown on top. Came out delicious .

This was a good idea. I did change the veggies though. I steamed fresh baby carrots, green beans and used mushrooms. I also caramelized 1/2 chipped brown onion with garlic and one tsp of butter and let that all marinate BEFORE adding the chicken in last with the soup. Also added 1/2 cup of cheddar cheese and the flavor was awesome! I believe it tastes better with FRESH veggie as opposed to canned. Definitely going to make this again.

I cooked the biscuits on top of the whole thing in a casserole dish. It turned out great!! I also didn't use a bag a frozen vegetables. I boiled sliced carrots, potatoes, and onion in pot of water and chicken Boyon. Then mixed them with the soup and chicken i used some of the flavored water to thin it down. The extra flavor was great.

Both my boyfriend and I love traditional chicken pot pie, but were looking for an option that we could make with less calories and fat. We found this deconstructed pot pie recipe and decided to give it a try. We used the lower fat version of the soup and frozen stew vegetables. We cooked the chicken in chicken broth versus oil and added garlic and onions to the skillet. Based on other reviews, we knew to add some spice. It turned out good, but could have used some additional spice. I also should have added some broccoli or cauliflower to the recipe. All in all, a good dish that I will try again.

This was awesome! My husband and teenage son loved it. I added cubed potatoes that had been partially boiled and also some salt, pepper, onion and garlic powder. Sooo good and easy - will be making again!

Very good base recipe that requires some tweaking depending upon your individual taste. I used 2 cans of the regular condensed cream of chicken soup, added thinly sliced carrots, peas and corn and a little chopped onion and about 1 1/2 tsp celery salt. I also added a little chicken broth to thin the mixture. It was a hit!!!

It was easy and fast- especially since I used a rotisserie chicken! The one down side was with only the cream of chicken soup it turned into a gelatinous ball and began to stick to the sauce pan badly. Using the can of soup as a measure I added one can of water- perfect consistency then and was able to simmer! I added some garlic powder as well- but that gets added to most everything I make. I’d like to try with more veggies but was in a rush so grabbed a mixed veggie bag and went with it. Overall good- not the most amazing but not bad for being ready in 20-30 minutes!

Very good, comfort food and super-easy to put together when using leftover chicken. I did sauté a bit of onion and celery before adding chicken and veggies and added salt, pepper and some pasta water to stretch the sauce. Served over wide noodles. Might consider adding a can of cream of celery soup to increase the sauce.

I wasn't into this recipe as much as I thought it would be. It was decent and I loved how fast and easy it came together. I think I just wasn't in love the cream of chicken in this. I think I might try it again but with some tweaks.

As written, bland, and just not very good flavor. Tried adding some salt, helped a little but not enough. Tried adding other spices that I had in my cabinet and didn't help either. I think a large part of the problem is we just didn't enjoy the flavor that the cream of chicken soup gave it.
Delicious

I love this quick, easy and inexpensive meal. I, like other reviewers add garlic and onion powder and a little dried parsley to the soup mixture with about a 1/2 can of milk to pep it up and make it saucier. Great with Pillsbury Grands buttery layers biscuits.

I followed the recipe with no modifications. It came out great. Was so easy and I just happened to have everything on hand. Worked out perfectly. Will keep this in the mental rolodex for future quick & easy meals.
Everyone loved this. I marinated the chicken with some garlic powder and soy sauce for 1/2 hour before. Will make this again.

It's a great idea, but the consistency is nothing like chicken pot pie. So, instead, I made my own as if it where going into a pie crust and put that over biscuits. Now, THAT was delicious. But, thank you for the idea. I also used potatoes, corn, green beans, carrots, etc for veggies. This recipe is so much better when it's authentic.

This recipe was nice to try and was very simple, but it left me wanting more flavor and wishing that I had just made chicken pot pies. Now don't get me wrong, it was so simple I still had to give it a shot but much better just to go the extra steps and even maybe just use a pre made pie crust for real pot pies. First of all there was barely any seasoning. So I added onion and garlic powder with some extra salt and pepper while cooking the chicken and after adding the veggies because it was so bland without. The other thing I ended up doing was adding chicken broth because the soup was not enough creaminess for even a fake pot pie. At least there is a simple thing to make if I need to go down this road again but unless I get desperate, I will not be making this again. Oh well, thanks for the thought!
Easy and tasty! Definitely will make it again!!
